_readme: Public-content guard rules - the STRUCTURAL layer.
Rules here are deliberately generic: path shapes, credential shapes and a
small vocabulary of internal-governance words. Project-private specifics
(real usernames, contact names, partner names) are NOT listed here - they go
in the optional local overlay named by EPHEMORA_PUBLIC_GUARD_RULES, which
stays out of the repository. Public CI runs only the patterns below. Findings
are verified and classified by a human, never blind-deleted.
A rule object carries 'id' and 'regex', plus an optional 'benign_users' list
for the personal-home-path rule. An optional '_note' key is prose for the
reader only - nothing else in a rule is read, so a note can never change

content_rules._note: benign_users lists only names that are structurally generic (CI runners, placeholders). It deliberately does NOT list an account name that a real reference host turned out to use, because that would silence exactly the build paths this rule exists to catch.

Work/research/governance identifier shapes found by the 1.2.0 pre-push sweep. The hyphenated form was covered; the shapes the tree actually carried (bare work-package numbers, hyphenated demo items, work-package-prefixed file names) were not, so the guard could not have caught its own release. Each class is a separate rule id so a finding names the family it belongs to.
A research-question reference is written as a work-package id, a slash and a Q-number; a roadmap quarter appears as ``Q3/2027``. Anchoring on the preceding slash keeps the second shape legal.

Lower-case work-branch names (wp-<item>-<topic>) recorded as the branch value of an evidence run. No public ref resolves them, and the digit-first form is what the identifier rule above does not match.

Environment names that raw captures inherit from the machine they were taken on: a build tree named after a numbered gate, and a laboratory host name. Both are private infrastructure metadata, not measurement.

Artifact labels that encode an internal work item: an image tag naming a gate build, a container or mount path carrying a milestone number. Digits that follow a separator without the two-letter work prefix are not matched.
German internal work-stream / work-package labels used as docstring headers. They name a private planning item rather than the code being described, and no existing rule matched the word.
